anojā.cp: fem. a plant with orange-coloured flowers.
anojā.p: [Anoja+a] (thī) CL=9 Anojā Devī, wife of King Mahākappina. This queen was named Anojāa because of her yellowish appearance due to previous merit. When King Mahākappina left the throne to go to the Blessed One to become a monk, she followed with her female attendants to become a monk like the King. On her arrival, she attained Sotāpatti Phala preached by the Buddha and attained monkhood after taking Uppalavanna Their as her preceptor.
pn:
Anojā 01. Wife of Mahā Kappina, while he was king, before he entered the Saṅgha. She had been his wife in former births as well and had helped him in his good works. In this age she was of equal birth with Mahā Kappina and became his chief consort. She was so-called because her complexion was the colour of anoja-flowers.

When Kappina made his renunciation, she and her companions followed him in chariots, crossing rivers by an act of truth (saccakiriyā), saying “the Buddha could not have arisen only for the benefit of men, but for that of women as well.”

When she saw the Buddha and heard him preach, she and her companions became Stream-enterers. She was ordained by Uppalavaṇṇā (AN-a.i. pp.176ff.; SN-a.ii., pp.178ff). In the Visuddhimagga it is said that Mahā Kappina was present when she heard the Buddha preach, but the Buddha contrived to make him invisible. When she asked whether the king was there, the Buddha’s reply was “Would you rather seek the king or the self?” “The self.” was the answer (p.393. The conversation on the “self.” seems to have been borrowed from Vin.i.23.

မဟာကပ္ပိနမင်း၏ မိဖုရား အနောဇာဒေဝီ။ ဤမိဖုရားသည် ရှေးကောင်းမှုအရ အနောဇပန်းကဲ့သို့ ဝါရွှေသော အဆင်းရှိသောကြောင့် အနောဇာဟူသော အမည်ကို ရသည်။ မဟာကပ္ပိနမင်းကြီး ထီးနန်းစွန့်၍ မြတ်စွာဘုရားထံ ရဟန်းပြုရန်ထွက်ခွါသွားသည်တွင် မိမိလည်း မင်းကြီးနည်းတူ ရဟန်းပြုရန် နောက်ပါ အမျိုးသမီး အခြံအရံနှင့် အတူ လိုက်သွား၍ ဘုရားရှင်ထံရောက်ရာ ဘုရားရှင်က တရားဟောသဖြင့် သောတာပတ္တိဖိုလ်သို့ ဆိုက်ရောက်ပြီးနောက် ဥပ္ပလဝဏ်ထေရီမကို ဥပဇ္ဈာယ်ပြု၍ ရဟန်းမဘဝကို ရသည်။

Anojā：1. Anojā.-Wife of Mahākappina，while he was king，before he entered the Order. She had been his wife in former births as well and had helped him in his good works. In this age she was of equal birth with Mahākappina and became his chief consort. She was so called because her complexion was the colour of anoja-flowers.

When Kappina made his renunciation，she and her companions followed him in chariots，crossing rivers by an act of truth （saccakiriyā），saying ”the Buddha could not have arisen only for the benefit of men，but for that of women as well.”

When she saw the Buddha and heard him preach，she and her companions became Stream-enterers. She was ordained by Uppalavannā （AA.i. pp.176ff. ； SA.ii.，pp.178ff）. In the Visuddhimagga it is said that Mahākappina was present when she heard the Buddha preach，but the Buddha contrived to make him invisible. When she asked whether the king was there，the Buddha’s reply was ”Would you rather seek the king or the self?” ”The self ” was the answer （p.393. The conversation on the ”self” seems to have been borrowed from Vin.i.23.
